entities.summary: The UNESCO Convention Against Discrimination in Education is a multilateral treaty which aims to combat discrimination in the field of education. It was adopted on 14 December 1960 in Paris and came into effect on 22 May 1962. The Convention ensures the free choice of religious education and private school, and the right to use or teach their own languages for national minority groups. The Convention prohibits any reservation. As of December 2025, 111 states were members of the Convention. It is the first international instrument which covers the right to education extensively and has a binding force in international law.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The UNESCO Convention Against Discrimination in Education has had a significant impact on promoting equality and inclusion in education globally, with 111 states as of December 2025. Its binding force in international law has helped establish the right to education as a fundamental human right.
